newsitem.title: CROATIA: Earthquake shakes buildings on Croatian coast.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake shakes buildings on Croatian coast.

text.p: An earthquake shook towns on Croatia's Adriatic tourist coast on Thursday night but there were no reports of casualties, state radio reported early on Friday.
The tremor hit at 10:44 p.m. (2044 GMT) and the epicentre of the tremor was about 30 km (20 miles) west of the Adriatic resort of Dubrovnik, the radio reported.
A seismologist at the U.S. geological survey said the earthquake measured a substantial 5.9 on the Richter scale.
"It was felt through a wide area," said John Minsch at the U.S. geological survey's national earthquake information centre in Golden, Colorado.

He said the earthquake hit near the shore at a shallow depth, increasing the likelihood of damage. He pinpointed its epicentre at latitude 42.85 degrees north, longitude 17.90 east, or about 15 miles (24 km) northwest of Dubrovnik.

The information centre in Dubrovnik said the tremor caused landslides near the epicentre, between the town of Ston and Dubrovnik, and knocked out power in Ston and at least one other regional centres.
Authorities said one woman was slightly injured in Slano, north of Dubrovnik, but there were no further details.
Kate Bobic of Ston said by telephone that aftershocks persisted more than an hour after the earthquake hit.
"Everything is still shaking," she said. "People are nervous. The entire town is spending the night in their cars... You cannot stay in a house during this."
Some residents estimated the earthquake lasted about a minute.
An employee of the Hotel Argentina in Dubrovnik's mediaeval old town said frightened residents rushed out of apartment buildings and gathered on the street after the quake struck.
"Nothing was falling down on our hands but everything shook. It lasted a long time," Petr Medilo told Reuters by telephone.
Residents in Ston said the tremor shattered roofs on older homes and knocked out power.
Croatian radio said the earthquake was also felt to the north on the Dalmatian islands of Brac and Hvar and inland at Imotski and Sinj.
Buildings were rocking back and forth in Makarska, a coastal town some 160 km (100 miles) north of Dubrovnik.
Aftershocks were reported at 11:45 p.m. in Makarska, the radio said. The tremor could be felt hundreds of kilometres (miles) to the west in the Bosnian capital Sarajevo.
